text: When an ice40 matmul at 2x2 PEs is feasible at 90.4 MHz with 4/8 DSPs and an output-control critical path, don't widen to 4 columns with dsp_regs=out and pipe_mul=1 just to fill the 8-DSP cap—it adds 150 LUTs and 4 DSPs and costs 9.1 MHz (to 81.3 MHz) because the critical path shifts to enable/control routing—unless the doubled MAC/cycle is essential.

On iCE40 matmul at the 8-DSP cap, when the critical path is the row-token/enable fabric route rather than the DSP accumulator, collapse the 2x4 PE array to 1x8 to keep 8 MAC/cycle while deleting row-select control, gaining +13.2 MHz (81.3→94.5 MHz) for +101 LUTs (305→406).

When an ice40 matmul at 2x2 PEs is feasible at 90.4 MHz with 4/8 DSPs and an output-control critical path, don't widen to 4 columns with dsp_regs=out and pipe_mul=1 just to fill the 8-DSP cap—it adds 150 LUTs and 4 DSPs and costs 9.1 MHz (to 81.3 MHz) because the critical path shifts to enable/control routing—unless the doubled MAC/cycle is essential.

On iCE40 matmul at the 8-DSP cap, when the critical path is the row-token/enable fabric route rather than the DSP accumulator, collapse the 2x4 PE array to 1x8 to keep 8 MAC/cycle while deleting row-select control, gaining +13.2 MHz (81.3→94.5 MHz) for +101 LUTs (305→406).

When an ice40 matmul already uses all 8 SB_MAC16s and timing is slack-rich (94.5 MHz vs 40 MHz target), strip per-PE fabric pipeline/enable and DSP-output registers while reshaping from 1x8 to 2x4 to cut 102 LUTs (406→304) at the same 8 DSPs, accepting the 16.3 MHz Fmax drop (to 78.2 MHz) because the new critical path shifts to out_valid routing and still clears target.

When an iCE40 8-MAC/cycle matmul is LUT-bound at 304 LUT with 40 MHz already met, don't transpose the PE array from 2x4 to 4x2 to reduce column enable/skew fan-out, because it only gains 3.7 MHz (78.2→82.0) while costing 50 LUT (304→354) with DSP unchanged at 8, since LUT scales per PE and the critical path stays routing-dominated.

When an ice40 matmul is throughput-pinned at 8 DSPs (8 MAC/cycle), already feasible at 82 MHz, and LUT-limited, register the A/B inputs at the 2x4 PE-array boundary so the input-distribution decode/mux collapses behind a flop, cutting LUTs 354→304 with Fmax unchanged at 82 MHz and DSPs unchanged at 8.

When an ice40 matmul is feasible at 90.4 MHz with only 4/8 DSPs and row-token/out_valid routing on the critical path, going to 8 MAC/cycle via a 2x4 PE array keeps Fmax flat (89.9 MHz, -0.5 MHz) at +250 LUTs but shifts the critical path to PE enable routing (5.33 ns route), so prefer deleting row-token/row-select control entirely to reach ~94.5 MHz for ~100 extra LUTs if enable/skew routing degrades.

When an ice40 matmul already meets the 40 MHz target with ~90 MHz Fmax and 8 DSPs but the critical path is control routing rather than the MAC, reshape the PE array from 1×8 to 2×4 and set reg_in=true to register A/B at the array boundary, collapsing the input-distribution decode/mux behind flops and cutting LUTs 405→304 while dropping Fmax only 89.9→82.0 MHz and preserving 8 MAC/cycle and feasibility.

When an ice40 matmul with DSP-combined accumulators is feasible at 82 MHz and routing-critical control, keep the 2x4 PE array instead of reshaping to 4x2, which adds 50 LUTs and drops Fmax to 76.1 MHz because the LUT4 control route grows from 5.4 to 6.4 ns.
